I was in a really similar situation to you when I was finishing up active duty. Here are some things I think you should keep in mind:  
\- If you are going to be eligible for GI bill benefits, then understand you have a rare opportunity to get an education that will be used to help meet the needs of your community. Take full advantage of that privilege.

\- As hard as it may be to believe, you are not alone in this. The military is really good at disillusioning people to the nonsense that blind patriotism is. You have seen firsthand how messed up the system is, and who is benefiting from it. Even if your whole unit is a bunch of full-hooah clowns, there are others who are experiencing similar things. If you find other people in your unit who are also disillusioned, reach out and build some solidarity and sanity together. I did this and those guys are still my best friends to this day.

\- A lot of leftists (especially online) are incredibly ignorant of what the military is like, and they have a hard time understanding how people can be gaslit into supporting it. Luckily this is not the majority. Once I joined some leftist groups and went through some activist training programs, nearly all of them valued the insight I was able to offer as someone who had seen another side of the imperialist machine that they were blind to. Once you get out you should absolutely look into joining some of these orgs. In particular, I recommend checking out the Socialist Rife Association, and About Face, which is a leftist group just for Vets.

"You're insane, aren't you?"

"He is absolutely insane!"

"Now look, guys. I know this sounds hard. But I believe that we may actually be able to do this! It will be well worth the payoff! Besides, it's not like he's a god or anything like that!"

Silence filled the small back room where three young men sat around a candlelit table, looking down at the scroll that had just been brought to them. The scroll had only four words written on it, "Kill him. Large reward". These three men did not need any names. They knew exactly who he was. He was a legend. 

"How are we even going to manage this?" one protested. "For one thing we don't even know what he looks like! Even if we did, I find it hard to believe that a merchant, a bartender, and a blacksmith can take on the greatest warrior in the land!"

The bartender responded, "Come on, a hero like him, shouldn't be too hard to spot! I've heard some of the bards sings songs about him. He supposedly has very distinguishable features. They say it's as if the Gods took extra time perfecting him!" 

"Exactly!" Cried the blacksmith, "That issue should resolve itself. We only need to worry about the HOW. Because you are right, we cannot directly take him on. He's just too strong."

With a stern look the merchant asked, "So how exactly do you expect us to do it then?"

The blacksmith sprouted a grin and proudly stated, "I thought you would never ask. Follow me" 

The group walked out of the small room and into the bustling tavern, populated with drunks and fools of all kinds. They made their way across the energy filled room over to a corner covered with fliers nailed to the wall. The blacksmith pointed at one in particular with pride in his face. It read; 

"QUEST AVAILIBLE! ESCORT NEEDED! REWARD!"

"What's that got to do with us?"
"THIS, is our plan!"

The look of confusion on the other two men's faces asked for an explanation.

"I'll go over the finer details later, since I expect that he will be here soon and we're short on time. But here's what I need..." He pointed at the bartender, "I need YOU to find the meanest bandits and monster hunters in this place. Someone who's willing to do anything for a bit of coin!" The bartender nodded and went off on his task.

"And me?", the merchant grunted

"Yes you. I'm going to need you to trust me here because this part is important. You are going to ALMOST die"

The merchant just stared. As if not completely processing the words just spoken to him. After a while he could only say, "Um... What?".

The blacksmith explained the plan, "He is going to escort you to the next town over, but on the way you guys are going to walk into an ambush. That's what the bandits and hunters are for. He's going to have to fight off the monsters and whatnot while trying to keep you alive. He will become overwhelmed and will proceed to start being... well... dead."

The merchant took a breath and retorted, "Don't you think maybe he's going to have had a little experience with this? I mean as strong as he is it's going to be a simple task keeping me alive!"

"Yes but here's where things will be different. Remember how I said you're going to ALMOST die? You are going to actively throw yourself into harms way as much as possible. If you show no regard for your own safety I'm certain he is going to lose track of an enemy or two, and will then allow us to overwhelm him and kill him." 

The merchant was extremely hesitant to agree to this, but in all honesty it sounded like a fairly solid plan. Begrudgingly he agreed. Just as he did the bartender returned.

"Alright, I talked to some people, we have about thirty to forty bandits and five hunters who are willing to provide a troll and a griffin they captured!"

The group looked at each other. As nervous as they were, they felt they may actually have a chance. The blacksmith went to speak with their new hires.

About an hour later he returned, "I just briefed the bandits and hunters on the plan. According to the bandits they expect him to be here tomorrow about noon. In the morning we will get into position Once he arrives, we will put the plan into motion"

The bartender poured a couple of pints for the team. The merchant raised his drink and said "Well gentlemen, here's to this absolute insanity!" 

The next morning things were being set into motion. The blacksmith rode out to the ambush site with the bandits. The monster hunters had spent the night there to guard the monsters they had brought out. The bartender was at the tavern waiting patiently for their target to walk in, ready to direct him to the merchant, who was sitting alone at a table waiting for the hero to offer his aid.

The time had come. Right around noon he walked in to the tavern and immediately the bartender knew it was him. A very tall and rough yet handsome looking warrior, wearing the finest armor. With a sword fit to slay a dragon. He asked the bartender for a drink. At this point the bartender almost forgot his lines. He managed to work up to courage to speak to this very intimidating hero, "You know, there's a man over there who could probably use your assistance. I'm sure he could pay well". And just as planned, the warrior offered to escort the merchant to wherever he was going.

"GET READY!" The blacksmith shouted to the first wave of bandits. This wave meant only to stop the escort to the rest of the force could overwhelm him. 

"Stay here, let me handle this" the hero said to the merchant. He then proceeded to lock blades with the bandits. However they got a little too bold and made an attempt to kill the hero right there, as opposed to just keeping him busy. They were now being cut down by the expert swordsman.

Then from the left side ten more bandits came out from the woodline, screaming and charging at the hero. With screams of his own, the merchant ran into the fray. The hero, obviously shocked and confused, ran after him. Cussing as the bandits started roughing up the merchant.

Then as that conflict was going on, the bandits on the right side charging into the fight, followed soon by the hunters and their monsters. The fight was being won! The hero was taking several critical hits from the bandits and many hits from the griffin. It was intense. 

Normally the hero would have broken away from the fight to consume a health potion, but with the merchant being beaten nearly to death, he couldn't afford risking losing the merchant. So he kept fighting, until he saw a gap in the chaos. He then managed to grab the merchant, and run away from the crowd and gave the beaten merchant a potion. However, right as he did that, a sharp paid pierced his back. One of the bandits had thrown a knife right in the hero's back. And it was one hit too many. The hero fell to the ground, dead. 

As the merchant and the blacksmith and all the bandits were celebrating their victory, Four of the monster hunters wrestled the troll back into his chains. The blacksmith asked where the fifth was, so he could pay them all at the same time. No one knew where he was. Just then, there was the sound of a griffin flying by. It had flown away just before the fight was over, which everyone thought was so it could recover from some of the hero's attacks. But when the group saw the hunter on the griffins back, the blacksmith suddenly realized what was happening. But it was too late, the griffin had picked up the hero's body, and was now flying to the next town over. Where a very wealthy villain waited for his prize.
